Community marketplace · UX/UI case study

Plant Stall

Helping plants find their next home.

A mobile marketplace for buying, selling, swapping, and giving away plants. Designed around the needs of new plant owners and experienced collectors.

Format
Mobile app
Focus
Research, user journeys, wireframes, UI design
01 Overview02 Decisions03 Design04 Reflection

01 / The context

The experience behind the screens.

Plant Stall explores a second-hand marketplace where a plant can be sold, exchanged, or shared. The project moves from research and personas through journey mapping, paper sketches, wireframes, and a nature-inspired interface.

The design challenge

A standard shopping flow does not cover every plant transaction. Beginners may be working with a small budget, while collectors need specific varieties, confidence in a plant’s condition, and a way to propose a swap.

02 / Design decisions

What shaped
the experience.

01

Let people explore first

Skippable onboarding and guest browsing let visitors see nearby and popular plants before creating an account.

02

Treat swapping as a core journey

An offer includes plant photos, seller details, and contact options. People can select their own plants to propose an exchange.

03

Support different kinds of value

Listings can be for sale, swap, or free. Negotiable and unspecified prices accommodate plants that are harder to price.

04 / Reflection

What this
work brings together.

The defining design decision is to support exchange alongside purchase. The case study brings research artifacts and interface decisions together; further validation should focus on whether buyers and sellers understand the proposed swap and pricing options.
